evidence.why: Launch assignments, state selection and all relevant local callbacks.
Pre-update threshold behavior rather than a hard clamp.
A true animation callback result destroys the item.
Reflection wrapper returns false after reorientation.

facts.rationale: Corrects the unsupported upward-launch assertion, makes the registered terminal event roles explicit, and distinguishes animation-driven destruction from a motion-state transition without assuming attribute values or a hard velocity clamp.
facts.value: Each successfully created star enters motion state 0 with X velocity equal to StarAttrs.speed times facing_dir and Y velocity copied from common attribute x18; this source does not establish the sign of that initial Y velocity. Physics applies the common sign-sensitive falling-speed threshold helper and adds StarAttrs.accel times current facing_dir to X velocity. The animation callback returns true when its JObj animation query becomes inactive, causing dispatcher destruction rather than a transition to another motion state. Damage-dealt, clank, absorption and ordinary shield-hit handlers run shared impact feedback and return true; separate shield-bounce and reflection callbacks return false through their shared responses. The collision callback performs shared stage processing and always returns false.
